title: The command center — three looks for the whole page, pick the feel

steps.path: The page you open in the morning, as it first appears
steps.headline: Which overall feel should the command center have?
steps.notice: Whichever you pick becomes the skeleton: the briefing, the map and the screen gallery all live on it. Every tag and count on these pages has a hover explanation; clicking a system opens its parts. The pictures are the first screen only.
steps.risk: All three are drawn from the same real data this morning, so the numbers are honest but the buttons do nothing yet.

variants.label: One page you scroll
variants.summary: Everything on one page, top to bottom: four numbers with buttons, what to pick up next, the efforts in flight, then eight system cards, then the screens. No tabs; you scroll.
variants.risk: The map's second row and the screens are below the fold, so the opening picture is mostly the briefing.

variants.label: The map is the room
variants.summary: The map fills the screen as a diagram with lines between the systems, counts on the lines; the morning list runs down the right side in your order; screens below.
variants.risk: Two lines cross near Foundations and one loops around the edge; a diagram with lines always has a few of these.

variants.label: Two lanes, three tabs
variants.summary: Three tabs: Today, Map, Screens. The map is two lanes, What you see above and Behind the scenes below, one column per system, with in-flight work pinned to the lane it lives in.
variants.risk: The most grid-like of the three; the briefing is a tab away rather than in view.
